item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
1. The color in the description doesn't match the picture.
  2. I think the caption should be changed from "rare" properties to "anomalous" or "unusual".
  3. On that note, it really is just an anomalous item as it's currently written.
  4. I don't see the issue with "magnetic east". If it just said "east", that would be a different direction since the magnetic poles do not perfectly line up with the geographic poles of the planet. It sounds weird because it isn't a term that's normally used, but it seems legitimate enough to me. Stating the rock "travels eastwardly perpendicular to the line demarcated between magnetic north and magnetic south" is far too wordy and overly verbose when you can say "magnetic east" and convey the same thing. Distaste for the term itself aside, did anyone have any trouble at all in understanding exactly what "magnetic east" meant? I doubt it.
  5. blazing_grey nailed on the head some things that would make it more interesting. A thought that occurred to me: if you hold it four feet off the ground and let go, does it stay four feet off the ground as it goes? If you drop it from six feet, etc? Does it tumble through the air, or is it "tidally locked" as it travels? Some sort of testing to show just how wacky it really is, and in what way, would help the article not come off so… blah.
  6. The bit about its recovery is so dull I don't care about it. I just don't. And the amount of expungement in that paragraph makes putting it there completely unnecessary. My exact thoughts reading that part were, "What's a Min Min Light? 'Black boxes, expunged data, document that doesn't exist.' Nevermind, I don't care about its recovery at all. I am bored by this paragraph."
  7. lolFoundation stealing items for personal use. There are a number of items that have been approved for somewhat regular use by personnel, so I wouldn't have an issue if Doctor Black box requested to use it as a sideways paperweight. But that little note basically says someone (or someones) can't be trusted to not steal an anomalous rock… so what else are they stealing from the Foundation?
  8. -1

item.content:encoded:
I personally have always smelled some additional creep with this one. It's falling around the earth. What happens if it completes an orbit? If allowed to fall through a long distance of vacuum, does it reach a terminal velocity, or just keep accelerating? If it does keep accelerating, while that's not enough to raise it to Euclid, it does seem to warrant a note about the danger of dropping this thing out a window resulting in earth gaining a constantly-accelerating satellite that eventually has so much relativistic apparent mass it collapses into a black hole and swallows the earth.

More interestingly, maybe it's not actually falling around the earth. Maybe it's falling "down" along the local gravity vector of…somewhere else. Not so much trying to get home as having never quite left…

item.content:encoded:
Overall, i like the concept of this one. I think in terms of whether it's an anomalous object or an scp, it could be both. On the one hand, it's not terribly bizzare and could fit in as just an anomalous object. On the other hand, it merits containment at some level, since a rock that drops sideways could have some significant danger. imagine this thing crashing into a crowd from a significant distance. Nasty.

On the issue of the supposed LOLFoundation, I'm of the opinion that this dosn;t qualify. It's not an example of people being stupid. There's no substantial danger in using this thing as a paperweight, so long as you're not engaging in something clearly stupid (using it right next to a window or door, etc.). And be honest, if you had this thing lying around, you'd use it to, until the boss chewed you out for it.

All that said, Should it be desired, i have an idea for a rewrite that would cement it as an scp and harden the science.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is actively bad. Too short, I don't think magnetic east is a thing that exists, the item is too boring, the tone is off (words like "simply," "ordinary", etc. don't belong in documents), and it ends in a goddamn humorous researcher note. Thanks to Mafia_Puppet for pointing this one out to me so I could cancel his/her/its vote.

edit: Let me explain the tone thing further:

For all intents and purposes, SCP-283 is an ordinary rock,

For all intents and purposes? If the thing is attracted to a gravitational field only it can detect based on a direction that doesn't exist, that is (to the extent that this shitty phrasing can imply such) an intent and purpose in which this is not an ordinary rock. So the phrase doesn't have any meaning here and should be replaced. The fact that it both doesn't apply and, in fact, actively contradicts the purpose of the document is indicative of the fact that "for all intents and purposes" is a colloquialism and doesn't belong in a scientific document. Try again.
